box.note: The light box is the page ground by default on every page, and in print in either scheme (@media print forces these aliases on :root).

film.note: The whole page turns to film under the system dark scheme; one static grain sheet (body::after) applies. No manual toggle, no per-page surface attribute.

plate.note: Every data plate (vessel viewer, FFR curve, spectrograms, CT phase scrubber, A+4DCT results, paper figures, the CV photo lightbox, the 404 frame) re-declares the film aliases, so plates are film in both schemes and in print.

print.note: Print is ink on white paper in either scheme; plates keep their film; the grain is removed.

bone-2.note: Secondary ink on film, held at 0.80 or lighter (Revision 2 dark floor).

bone-3.note: 0.64 clears 4.5:1 on film-0 and film-1 (5.85:1 and 5.26:1).

colormaps.name: turbo
colormaps.note: Google polynomial approximation; one shared p range for CFD and PINO.

colormaps.name: diverging
colormaps.note: Moreland cool-warm; symmetric about zero; values past +absMax take the over color.

colormaps.name: viridis
colormaps.note: Degree-6 polynomial fit of matplotlib viridis.

name.purpose: The home h1 (the owner's name); Archivo width 92, clamp(2.25rem, 1.5rem + 2.6vw, 3.5rem).

title.purpose: Home section headings (Work, Selected) over a hairline; CV section headings over a primary-ink rule.

row-title.purpose: Work names, selected-paper titles, CV entry titles; Archivo 600, 0.975-1.0625rem.

body.purpose: Research paragraphs (60ch), Updates sentences, Work clauses; the tagline and CV intro at 1.125rem; 1rem at 640px and under.

caption.purpose: Figure and table captions; italic STIX in ink-2; 0.9rem at 640px and under.

ui.purpose: Nav, buttons, the identity role line, the Method and metrics rows.

mono.purpose: Numbers, units, identifiers, DOIs, years, tables and link rows: identity and footer link rows, Updates dates, project years and outputs lines, CV periods, counts, contact and jump rows, metrics tables, BibTeX, the colophon. Never prose. 0.8rem on the box, 13px (0.8125rem) on film.

label.purpose: Corner chrome, colorbar labels, tags, the wipe grip; 0.75rem on the box, 13px (0.8125rem) on film; uppercase only for short unit-free identifiers.

name-ko.purpose: profile.nameKo beside the home h1 on the same baseline, ink-2, lang=ko; a Pretendard Medium subset of only those glyphs (scripts/subset-name-ko.py), preloaded.

summary.purpose: The one STIX sentence under a research project title; 1rem at 640px and under.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system is flat. Separation is a 1px hairline in --line or a one-step tonal lift to --bg-1.

shadows.name: segment-pressed-underline
shadows.purpose: A 2px signal underline on a pressed segmented button, drawn as an inset box-shadow. An underline, not an elevation.

texture.name: film-grain
texture.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.9, 2 octaves, desaturated, 256px tile, opacity 0.05, position fixed
texture.purpose: One static grain sheet over the page under prefers-color-scheme: dark only (body::after); none on the light box; never animated; removed in print.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Hovers and state changes (color, border, underline), caret turns, the skip link, the lightbox fade-out.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Reveals: a fold a reader clicks eases its height (Updates, Method and metrics, CV phone folds; ::details-content, gated by data-motion); the lightbox fade-in; the viewer canvas, handle and segments fade in at ready; the home poster fades out after a 250ms delay.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: The two-state CFD | PINO wipe tween on narrow frames.

motion.name: duration-develop
motion.purpose: The PINO layer develops over the CFD field once, on first visibility, for the measured inference time; snaps under reduced motion.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Idle drift on every vessel viewer, home plate included; paused offscreen, on document.hidden and during drags; stops only under prefers-reduced-motion. scene.ts holds the period as a constant; the --drift-period token is declared but not read.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for every transition.

breakpoints.name: zoom-200
breakpoints.purpose: A phone at 200% zoom: nav wraps, home portrait under the lead, figures, Method and metrics rows and projects take one track, outputs and talk formats may break inside, viewer field toggle wraps, every other tick on colour scales and time axes, dB scale halves, metric values under their labels, CV header stacks.

breakpoints.name: nav-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Nav gaps 1rem, type 0.875rem; the four items fit one row at 390px.

breakpoints.name: table-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Metrics tables stack each metric as a block; CV citations use the venue code and the DOI the word DOI.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The disclosure layer: identity compact (4rem portrait, short role line, address on its own line), Updates stacked, Work rows hidden, Selected DOI as the word, outputs line folded behind a caret, CV jump row and folds, prose one size smaller.

breakpoints.name: viewer-rows
breakpoints.purpose: Viewer: the wipe handle gives way to a two-state toggle; in chapter plates the colorbar and controls move into rows under the canvas.

breakpoints.name: cv-stack
breakpoints.purpose: CV period rows and skills to one column; talks and patents put their meta under the title; CV portrait 4rem; photos 96px.

breakpoints.name: home-rows
breakpoints.purpose: Work rows to one column; the home plate goes 3:4 at the full column width with the portrait poster.

layout.widthFrame: clamp(50rem, 58vw, 64rem), one centred fluid column for every block
layout.homePlate: 2:1 at the column width, max-height 60vh, min-height 16rem; 3:4 at full column width under 900px
layout.homeOrder: identity block, closed Updates row, plate and its STIX sentence, Work, Selected
layout.homeBudget: <= 250 visible words in <main>; a closed <details> counts only its <summary> (scripts/budget.mjs)
layout.researchProjectPad: 4rem above each project (3rem at 640px and under)
layout.leftEdge: One left edge and one right edge: every block spans the column; text narrows by measure only.
layout.mailtoBudget: at most 3 mailto: per page (nav Email, the address as text, the footer address), 0 on redirect stubs, every target profile.email
layout.cvHeader: 80px portrait, the name as h1, the intro line (interestsLine, #interests), two role lines, then the mono contact row on screen and in print (address as text, Google Scholar, ORCID, host).

formatting.unitJoin: U+202F narrow no-break space between value and unit and as thousands separator (8 649)
formatting.range: en dash, one trailing unit (10.7–13.0 kPa)

precision.quantity: FFR Pd/Pa (metrics tables: PINO case column and FFR MAE, A+4DCT no-script table; CFD-PINO difference)

formatting.manuscriptStatus: manuscript under revision (EAAI): printed once per entry (CV publications; on /research inside the outputs line).
formatting.doi: doi:<identifier>, lowercase, no space, mono, linked to https://doi.org/
formatting.proseCounts: numberWord: counts in ledes spelled as words
formatting.voice: First person, present tense, plain, for copy that speaks for the owner (tagline, footer line, research paragraphs); third person for author lists and collaborators.
formatting.cfdReference: CFD up to 35 min on 64 CPU cores (owner): a measured bound; never converted to hours or extrapolated to fewer cores; no speed-up factor above "about 1,000x".
formatting.framing: Organ-agnostic: computational hemodynamics · physics-informed AI · wearable biosignals · medical devices; coronary only where a coronary result is named.
formatting.shortVenue: A printed short venue over 14 characters fails the build (schema.ts VENUE_MAX).

narrative.northStar: The Light Box and the Film
narrative.overview:
The world is the cath-lab reading room: a light box with angiographic film clipped to it. The page is the light box, white and quiet, carrying who he is and the record in rows. The research is the film: every data artifact (the vessel viewer, the FFR curve, the spectrograms, the CT phase scrubber, the A⁺4DCT results chart) is a dark film plate with a hairline, sitting on the box. Nothing decorative competes with the plates; UI chrome is thin and mono, so it reads as instrument marking rather than interface.

Three pages. `/` is a Read surface, identity first: the name with the Korean name beside it, the role line with the four fields, the owner's one sentence, the address and the profile links, then one closed Updates row, then one quiet live plate and the sentence under it, then the Work rows and three selected papers. `/research` is an Experience surface: every research project in one flat list, newest first, each a title with its years, one sentence and an outputs line that links into the CV; three of them carry live demos (PINO, 4D CT, fluid bolus) whose plates stay in view while the method and metrics fold into one row closed at every width, one carries the A⁺4DCT results plate and two carry a paper figure. There is no citation line: the outputs line links each paper's CV row. `/cv` is the whole record, dense: rows, not frames. `/publications` and `/record` are meta-refresh redirects to `/cv/#publications` and `/cv/#talks`.

The ground follows the system scheme. The light box is the default; `prefers-color-scheme: dark` turns the whole page to film. Plates are film in both schemes, so in dark mode a plate is film on film, separated by its hairline. There is no manual toggle and no per-page surface switch. Components read semantic aliases only (`--bg`, `--ink`, `--line` and their tiers), which the scheme resolves for the page and the `.plate` scope re-declares to film for a plate. Print is ink on white paper in either scheme.

Rank is carried by border ink, never by weight, fill or color flooding. First-author work carries a primary-ink border on its role mark; co-first a secondary-ink border; co-authored a hairline. Signal never marks rank. Type weight stays even (one heading weight, 600), so the eye ranks by geometry.
keyCharacteristics: Light box by default, film under the dark scheme; data plates are film in both. One ink family per ground, one clinical red on both.
Identity first: the name is the h1; the plate is the one live proof near the top of home, quiet (pressure only, the CFD | PINO wipe, the colorbar, the idle drift).
Rows, not frames, for everything that is a record: the Updates row, the Work rows and selected papers on home, the outputs lines on /research, dense CV rows on /cv.
One centred fluid column for every block; text narrows by measure, never by a narrower box.

Three faces with fixed jobs: Archivo (width 92 for the name and page titles) for naming and UI, STIX Two Text for reading, JetBrains Mono for numbers, units, identifiers, DOIs, years, tables and link rows; a Pretendard subset only for the Korean name.
Phones (640px and under) are a disclosure layer over the same HTML, never a different site.
Flat throughout; depth is a hairline or a one-step tonal lift, plus one static grain sheet on a film page.
Signal red is reserved: probes, the PINO trace and the A⁺4DCT marks, active underlines, focus rings, selection, the hover state of icons and underlines, and the one primary action (the nav's Email).
Motion is physical evidence and quiet state: the PINO layer develops over the measured 1.78 s once, the vessel drifts, folds ease their height; reduced motion stops all of it.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Each ground has exactly one ink family in three tiers (box-ink on the light box, bone on film), plus the one signal red. No other UI color exists; colormaps belong to the data.

rules.name: The Alias Rule
rules.body: Components read `--bg`, `--bg-1`, `--bg-2`, `--line`, `--line-soft`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--ink-3` only. `:root` resolves them to the light box; `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` resolves them to film; `@media print` forces the light set back on `:root`; `.plate` re-declares them to film (with `color-scheme: dark` and the film mono and label sizes) for a plate in either scheme and in print. Raw `film-*` and `box-*` values are referenced directly only where an element must hold the other ground inside a plate (the scrubber's light-box sheet).

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate is any element in the `.plate` scope that holds a viewer, a chart, a spectrogram, a CT frame, a paper figure or an enlarged photograph (`<Frame plate>`, the paper-figure image, the CV lightbox dialog). It is film in both schemes: dark film on the light box, film on film (separated by its hairline) in dark. Nothing that is not data or an image sits on film.

rules.name: The Light-Box Rule
rules.body: White inside a film plate is the light box of the world, never a bare rectangle: it carries a hairline and mono corner chrome or a caption, and holds only a raster from the paper or the data, composited with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so the figure's own white becomes the box ground (normal blending under forced colors).

rules.name: The Signal-Is-A-Stroke Rule
rules.body: Signal red is a border, underline, ring, curve, data mark or icon state. Under text it is a fill only on the nav's Email action and the skip link, and then as `signal-fill`.

rules.name: The Dark Floor Rule
rules.body: On film, secondary ink is no darker than 0.80 lightness and mono and label type never fall below 13px. Every text and ground pair holds at least 4.5:1 in both schemes.

rules.name: The One Grain Rule
rules.body: A film page (the dark scheme) carries exactly one grain layer, applied by `body::after`: a static feTurbulence sheet tiled at 256px at 5% opacity, never animated, removed in print. The light box carries none, and plates add none of their own.

rules.name: The Mono Number Rule
rules.body: Numbers, units, identifiers, DOIs, years, tables and link rows are set in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals; `code`, `time` and `data` inherit it globally. Prose is never mono: a measured value inside a STIX caption is wrapped in `.num` but reads in the caption's own face.

rules.name: The One Formatter Rule
rules.body: A precision is a property of the quantity, not of the page: kPa at one decimal, FFR at two (three in metrics tables), seconds at two, mm at one.

rules.name: The Even Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings carry one weight (600), UI 500, body 400. Rank is carried by size, measure and border ink, never by bolding (the owner's name in an author list is the one bold).

rules.name: The Unit Keeps Its Case Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is chrome for short identifiers (C1, J2) and tags; units and ratios are never uppercased or tracked.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Every block (nav, identity, Updates, plates, rows, tables, footer) starts and ends where the column does. Measure is the only thing that narrows text; a centred narrower box, a centred plate or an indented caption breaks the rule.

rules.name: The One Target Rule
rules.body: A link target appears once per page in the human layer, and an action word once per viewport. Each Work row links its own research project (`#lbm-ctffr`, `#pino`, `#viscosity`, `#ffr-simulator`) and nothing repeats one; the sticky nav carries Email and CV on every page. A page carries at most three `mailto:`: the nav's Email, the address written as text (home identity row) and the footer's address; a redirect stub carries none; every target is `profile.email`; `scripts/budget.mjs` fails the build otherwise.

rules.name: The Two Things Rule
rules.body: The human layer is short and uneven: two big things (the identity block and the plate on home; the artifacts on research), everything else as rows. The machine layer (markdown twins, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `cv.json`, JSON-LD) is complete.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line or a tonal step. The only `box-shadow` in the build is the inset 2px signal underline on a pressed segmented button (viewer and scrubber), an underline by another property.

rules.name: The One Anatomy Rule
rules.body: A paper reads the same everywhere (home Selected, the CV): title (linked to the DOI when one exists), venue in mono, role mark, `doi:`. A role mark, tag or label never sits directly above a heading.

dos: Do lead home with who this is: the name as the h1 with the Korean name beside it, the role line, the four fields, the tagline, the address and profile links, then the closed Updates row and the quiet plate.
Do span every block across the one centred column and narrow text by measure (ch) only.
Do put every data artifact on a film plate (`Frame plate`), in both schemes.
Do keep records as rows: Updates, Work and Selected on home, outputs lines on /research, dense rows on /cv.

Do keep Email to the nav's one primary action and CV to the nav's page link on every page; the footer carries the address and LinkedIn, Google Scholar and ORCID minus whatever the last viewport already shows (`omit`).
Do ship every disclosure closed (Updates, Method and metrics) or open-and-folded-by-script (the CV phone folds) as a native `<details>` with the Phosphor caret, and keep the server HTML whole.
Do keep the idle drift on everywhere, home plate included; only reduced motion stops it.
Do read only the semantic aliases in components, so they work on the light box, on a film page, on a plate and in print.
Do set numbers, units, identifiers, DOIs, years, tables and link rows in JetBrains Mono, computed from content.ts or a manifest and formatted by `lib/format.ts`.
Do carry rank by border ink: primary ink for first author, secondary ink for co-first, hairline for co-author; never signal.
Do draw field colors from `lib/colormaps.ts` only, with five ticks on every bar and the error field on its fixed symmetric scale.
Do print nothing while a plate loads, and only its approved sentence when it fails.
Do honor `prefers-reduced-motion` on every autonomous motion.
Do describe the work organ-agnostically (computational hemodynamics, physics-informed AI, wearable biosignals, medical devices); coronary appears only where a coronary result is named.
donts: Don't switch a page's ground by attribute or add a theme toggle; the system scheme decides, and plates are always film.
Don't print a contact or CV action twice in one viewport: no Email button or CV (PDF) in the identity block or the footer, no per-project or per-entry mail links, no closing contact block.
Don't link a home target twice, or turn a count into a link.
Don't put mono type in prose, or a `key value · key value` readout string where a sentence belongs.
Don't print a case id, file name, array name or other dataset identifier in visible text, a caption or a failed plate.
Don't stack labels over a result ("what / result / consequence") or write consequence sentences; a demo project is its plates in view and one closed Method and metrics row.
Don't frame a record; frames are for data.
Don't use drop shadows, glows, gradients outside colormaps, blur or translucent panels.
Don't add kickers, eyebrows or section numbers above headings.
Don't introduce a second accent or a fourth ink tier.
Don't uppercase a unit or a ratio or track it.
Don't fill a role mark or tag.
Don't use icon fonts or glyph characters as icons; icons are inline Phosphor SVGs sized to the text.
Don't print a manuscript's status twice, as a tag, or in another wording.
Don't set mono or label type below 13px on film, or secondary ink darker than 0.80 on film.
Don't state a speed-up factor larger than "about 1,000x", convert the CFD bound into hours, or extrapolate it to fewer cores.
